script.base: CIN Bengals at MIA Dolphins, Week 5. Spread and total were not saved, so this CIN-MIA script is form-only and does not claim who the book expects to lead. CIN weeks 2-4 were pass-led: Tee Higgins 33 targets, 342 yards, 404 air yards, JaMarr Chase 24/200/192, Chase Brown 42 carries for 151 (3.6 YPC). MIA weeks 2-4 were run-led and pass-inefficient: Ollie Gordon 29/148 (5.1 YPC), DeVon Achane 23/91, Malik Willis 13/73, while Chris Bell had 208 air yards for only 67 yards and Kevin Coleman 8 targets for 6 yards. Base script: a competitive CIN-MIA game in which Joe Burrow keeps throwing to Higgins and MIA stays on the ground with Gordon, because the CIN defense allows 4.86 YPC and the MIA QB has not earned a pass-heavy script (EPA +0.01 with no blitz, -0.34 vs blitz) while CIN blitzes only 16%.

script.flip2: CIN pass game pulls ahead and MIA abandons the run. Gordon 9.7 carries a game disappear, Willis rushes become scrambles rather than a MIA handoff plan, and both passing games stay live so CIN Higgins keeps the air yards and MIA Malik Washington (20 targets, 166 yards) is the outlet.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both CIN-MIA legs lost. Higgins finished under 51.5 because the 342 yards were one blow-up the pack cannot split out, MIA blitzed near 29%, and Burrow -0.13 EPA versus pressure turned the CIN plan into Brown and Gesicki checkdowns. Brown already has 18 targets at -8 air yards, so Higgins never saw 11 targets. Gordon finished under 42.5 because Achane 23 carries and Willis 13 rushes were a MIA committee, not a Gordon feature, and once MIA trailed CIN they stopped the 9.7 carries that produce 49 yards. Six carries at 5.1 YPC is about 31. The Higgins counter is weaker than the read: a cut to 8 targets at 7 yards per target is still 56, and nothing in the pack says the CIN role shrank. The Gordon counter is closer, only a 7-yard cushion in a shared MIA backfield, which is why that leg is a lean tied to the base script. Neither counter is stronger than its read, so neither leg is dropped.
slip_story: One CIN-MIA story: a competitive mixed game, not a shootout and not a clock-grind. CIN keeps throwing to Higgins because that is how the Bengals have moved the ball (33 targets, 404 air yards), and MIA keeps handing Gordon the ball because Bell (208 air yards, 67 receiving yards) and Coleman (8 targets, 6 yards) have not earned a pass-heavy Dolphins script and CIN allows 4.86 YPC. The two legs win together in that base script. They split on flip 1 (MIA grind: Gordon hits, Higgins dies) and on flip 2 (CIN pulls away: Higgins can still hit, Gordon dies), so this is a base-script slip, not a blowout stack. Do not add a total (not saved), a TD, a reception, or a second market on either player. MIA Washington over 46.5 and CIN Brown rush yards under 64.5 were the next reads and were left off to hold two legs and one story.
